values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/kinglake ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (King Lake State Forest Campground, Baraga: 6 sites, $20), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Boat launch on King Lake, suited to smaller fishing boats and carry-in craft.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/kinglake ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.' 'There is a boat launch on King Lake. This launch is ideal for smaller fishing boats and carry-in access.'), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/kinglake ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.') + amenity table (King Lake State Forest Campground: 'Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com' no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Six sites 'for tent and small trailer camping' (the DNR's standard state forest wording; no maximum length posted). One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/kinglake ('Discover a rustic campground with six sites for tent and small trailer camping'; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + amenity table (6 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic state forest campground on the north shore of 498-acre King Lake, 14.8 mi E of Covington via US-141 N, US-41 S and King Lake Road (Baraga County); managed by Baraga State Park. Rocky islands to paddle among; bass, pike, perch and crappie; moose, eagles and loons often seen. Long narrow drive in: fine for a 23-ft rig, not for big rigs. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 6 tent/small-trailer sites (confirmed), $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only, 15-day maximum (all confirmed). Season: the amenity table says only 'weather dependent', so none written. Phone 906-353-6558 matches (Baraga SP). Not equestrian. Note trimmed of field restatements.
